text:
The details in your message came through as unfilled template brackets, so I don't have the real facts. I'd rather not invent a buildbot story or lessons that go out under your name to your network.

Could you send:

1. How many engineers are on the team
2. The old and new CI providers
3. What happened with the buildbot dashboard, even roughly, such as what broke, who noticed, and how it played out
4. Your 2-3 lessons, in your own words
5. Optionally, one thing you got wrong during the migration, if it's not already the dashboard story

Once I have those, I'll write the ~150-word post, with just the post text and nothing else.
sent:
I'm posting on LinkedIn about what our small team learned migrating our CI to a new provider, and I want it to read like a person wrote it, not an AI. The post goes out under my name to my professional network.

Details to work from:
- Team: small, [number] engineers
- Moved from: [old CI provider] to [new CI provider]
- The buildbot dashboard thing: [one or two sentences on what happened with the buildbot dashboard]
- Main lessons: [2-3 lessons, in my words]

Write one LinkedIn post of about 150 words in the first person, in plain conversational language, like a colleague telling a story over coffee. Use short and long sentences mixed together, and include one concrete detail or a small admission of something we got wrong. Leave out corporate buzzwords, "excited to share", "game-changer", "journey", and tidy three-part lists. Include the buildbot dashboard story as the memorable moment. Use no hashtags, no emojis, and no headings or bullets, so it reads as a few short paragraphs of plain text. End with one genuine question that invites readers to share their own CI migration experience, because I want comments.

Reply with the post text only, with no preamble, no word count, and no alternatives. Nothing follows the closing question.
